Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee twisting injury
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Reciprocal pivot shift injury pattern with osteochondral impaction injury at the lateral femoral condyle and osseous contusion at the posterior lateral tibial plateau. Mild osseous contusion at the posterior and peripheral medial tibial plateau. Mild osseous contusion at the proximal fibula. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion, mildly hyperintense on T1-weighted images, indicating a component of hemarthrosis. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete, acute tear of the ACL.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 sprain pattern edema about the MCL.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Pivot shift mechanism injury with:

-Osteochondral impaction injury at the lateral femoral condyle and osseous contusion at the posterior lateral tibial plateau.
-Mild osseous contusions at the posterior and peripheral medial tibial plateau and at the proximal fibula.
-Complete, acute tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
-Grade 1 sprain of the MCL.
-Small hemarthrosis.

In the medial compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. A intact8 cm subchondral bone cyst at anteormedial tibial plateau is noted.  
 The lateral compartment, there is longitudinal vertical tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is partial tear (low grade) of the anterior cruciate ligament at mid substance. High grade partial tear with some scarring of the posterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
 There is partial tear of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers). Partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament is present. There is partial tear of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance. Partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon. Tears of the meniscopopliteal fasicles are noted. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal.   -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
 -- Longitudinal vertical tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
 -- Partial tear (low grade) of the anterior cruciate ligament at mid substance.  
 -- High grade partial tear with some scarring of the posterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
 -- Posterolateral corner injury by evidence of  
 -- Partial tear of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance.  
 -- Partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon.  
 -- Tears of the meniscopopliteal fasicles.

COMPARISON:Prior imaging in back to [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Progressive right knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Inferiorly surfacing oblique tear posterior horn medial meniscus extending into the body, which is peripherally extruded. There is a superimposed complex tear of the posterior root. The anterior horn is intact.

Complex tear posterior root and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with peripheral extrusion of the lateral meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without intervertebral translation. There is a low-grade partial-thickness tear of the posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Severe popliteus tendinosis without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. Moderate pretibial superficial bursitis.

There is generalized thinning of patellofemoral articular cartilage with focal full thickness cartilage denuding along the lateral patellar facet near the patellar apex. There is thinning of lateral femorotibial articular cartilage. There is thinning of medial femorotibial articular cartilage.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex medial meniscal tear with medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Complex lateral meniscal tear with lateral meniscal extrusion.
3. Chronic complete anterior cruciate ligament tear without tibial translation.
4. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the posterior cruciate ligament.
5. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
6. Moderate tricompartment chondrosis consistent with moderate tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.

COMPARISON:Prior imaging in back to [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Medial joint line pain right knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. Mild prepatellar/pretibial superficial soft tissue edema. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 7 mm, within normal limits.

Trace knee joint fluid. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis with subtle areas of cartilage thinning overlying the patellar articular surface. Mild to moderate lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Preserved medial femorotibial articular cartilage. 

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of discrete meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.
2. Subtle chondrosis as detailed above, which may reflect evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.

> MRI of right knee was performed in sagittal, axial and coronal sections.
> Spin echo sequence were used.

A well-defined eccentric bony lesion in the epidiaphysis of right medial aspect of tibia and involving subarticular surface and cortical scalloping; the lesion showing lobulated apperance with internal septums and some hypointensity margin; heterpgenous hypointensity on T1WI and heterogenous hyperintensity on T2WI with some fluid-fluid interface and ill-defined hypointensity area inside, R/O giant cell tumor with internal hemorrahge maybe due to aneurysmal bone cystic change; the tumor size about 5*4*3.4 cm in size.
Increased singal intenisty of the articular cartilage of proximal tibia on T2WI, in favor of chondromalacia.
Adjancent bone marrow edema at right tibial plateua
Suspicious of prominent vessels in medial aspect of infrapatellar region.

Impression: R/O giant cell tumor in right proximal tibia with internal hemorrahge and perifocal bone marrow edema, maybe due to secondary aneurysmal bone cystic change.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 2 months of knee pain after slipping on stairs at work.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. T2 hyperintense signal at the medial femoral condyle, consistent with osseous contusion. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Low-grade chondral lesion in the distal femoral diaphysis.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the posterior horn without extrusion. No flipped fragments. No parameniscal cyst.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Oblique tear of the posterior horn without extrusion. No flipped fragments. Parameniscal cyst adjacent to the body measuring 1.1 x 1.6 cm.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Increased signal in the proximal fibular collateral ligament, consistent with prior injury. No tear.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Globular T1 hyperintense and T2 hyperintense lesion within the superolateral Hoffa's fat pad measuring 1.2 x 2.1 x 2.5 cm. The lesion abuts the cartilage surface of the patella and lateral trochlea.
Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Globular T2 hyperintense lesion within the superolateral Hoffa's fat measuring 2.5 cm. Differential diagnosis includes fat pad impingement, localized nodular synovitis, amongst other etiologies. Biopsy is recommended.
2.	Osseous contusion of the anterior medial femoral condyle.
3.	Oblique tear of the lateral meniscus posterior horn without extrusion.
4.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus posterior horn without effusion.
